In-ovo sexing advances across the US

The US egg industry is entering a new phase in hatchery management as in-ovo sexing moves from pilot projects to commercial production. Widely adopted in parts of Europe, the approach identifies an embryo's sex before hatch and is attracting growing interest from producers seeking to balance welfare commitments with operational and market realities.

Sunita van Es-SahotaEditor Poultry World

Nov 3

Article

In-ovo sexing is beginning to take hold in the US egg industry as producers look for ways to address the culling of male chicks. Photo: Bert Jansen 

The debate over in-ovo sexing begins with an uncomfortable reality in egg production. Male chicks from layer breeders do not lay eggs and are generally not suited to conventional broiler production, so they have traditionally been culled shortly after hatch.

The technology which identifies the sex of an egg before hatch is still in the early stages in the US market, but it is no longer hypothetical. Speciality producers are beginning to use it, retailers are signalling interest, and industry groups are increasingly treating it as a practical issue rather than a distant innovation. What remains unclear is how quickly the technology can move from early adoption to broader industry standard.

Europe, by contrast, has moved further and faster, helped by regulation and stronger policy pressure in several markets. That contrast is shaping the US discussion, where adoption so far has been driven less by law and more by a mix of retailer expectations, producer strategy, and consumer response.

A welfare issue

At the PEAK 2026 panel discussion earlier this year, Nancy Roulston, senior director of corporate policy & animal science at ASPCA, described in-ovo sexing as “the solution to ending male chick culling.” She called it a rare animal-welfare issue that is “completely preventable and entirely solvable within just a few years.”

The principle is straightforward: identify male embryos before hatch and remove them earlier in the incubation period. The technical challenge is determining sex reliably, at sufficient speed and without disrupting hatchery operations. That challenge has shaped the market’s development. 

Larry Sadler, vice president of animal welfare at United Egg Producers, said early promises had not always translated into commercially viable systems, but that the technology had now advanced to the point where several companies were operating in the market. Casey Downey, programme director at Innovate Animal Ag, mentioned 3 companies (AAT, Orbem and Seleggt) that had produced systems that were “commercially successful and commercially available in the market.” Two more companies join these 3: Omegga and Nectra.

Early US adoption

The United States currently has 6 commercial in-ovo sexing installations in operation, with egg producers representing more than 4% of the national layer flock committing to transition as existing flocks are replaced, according to the latest in-ovo sexing market penetration report from Innovate Animal Ag. 

Eggs from hens hatched using in-ovo sexing technology are already reaching US consumers through NestFresh's Humanely Hatched label and Kipster. Early adoption by these speciality egg producers has helped bring the technology into the mainstream, prompting larger industry players to assess the potential impact on their production practices and brand positioning. At the time of the report's publication, additional specialty egg companies, including Sauder's Eggs and Vital Farms, had announced plans to transition their flocks to in-ovo sexing.

Early male egg identification helps hatcheries reduce labour costs and free up valuable incubator and setter space. Photo: Orbem

NestFresh was among the first American producers to commercialise eggs from in-ovo sexed flocks. The company launched its Humanely Hatched brand and is now moving beyond its initial speciality lines.

Michael Sencer, senior vice president of NestFresh, said the company’s brown-egg focus made it a natural fit for AAT’s Cheggy, the system it selected. “Cheggy only works on brown chickens and is also the only one that operated at higher speeds to help keep the cost down,” he said. “We have not raised our prices for the process.”

He stated that the transition has taken time and investment. Sencer added that the company planned to complete its in-ovo sexing transition by the end of 2026 across NestFresh and selected speciality brands, before extending the approach to private-label customers.

Europe’s progress

Europe remains the leading market. According to the market penetration report, more than 281 million male embryos have been identified and removed before hatching globally since 2021 (Figure 1). Of the 328 to 346 million commercial laying hens in production in the EU, 125 to 142 million of them were sexed with in-ovo technology, implying a market penetration of 36.2 to 43.3%. This is up from 34% in April 2025. This significant increase coincided with the rapid expansion of in-ovo sexing capacity across Europe between late 2023 and mid-2025.

Figure 1 – 281 million male chicks in-ovo sexed globally as of 1 June 2026

The rollout of in-ovo sexing technology across the EU has accelerated rapidly, demonstrating its ability to meet demand in some of the world's largest egg-producing markets. Over the past 4 years, the number of female chicks produced annually using the technology has increased at an annual growth rate of 74%. In the 12 months to June 2026, in-ovo sexing systems produced 92 million female chicks (Figure 2), while installed capacity (at the time the market penetration report was published) exceeded 100 million female chicks per year.

Figure 2 – Female day-old chicks produced in the EU with in-ovo sexing

Italy's planned ban on male chick culling is set to become the next major driver of growth for in-ovo sexing in Europe. When the legislation takes effect in January 2027, Italy will join Germany and France in mandating alternatives to male chick culling, while the Netherlands continues its industry-led transition. Together, these markets represent 50.9% of the EU population. Because new regulations affect only newly-hatched chicks, the transition will occur gradually as laying flocks are replaced over an estimated 18-month production cycle, leading to a steady increase in market penetration rather than an immediate surge. Looking beyond Europe, in Switzerland, where in-ovo sexing technology kicked off in 2025, adoption now sits at around 85-100% of the country’s layer flock, while Norway has passed 50% and is moving toward a complete phase-out of male chick culling by 2027.

Technology and hatchery efficiency

Orbem’s AI-enabled MRI in-ovo sexing system, the Genus Focus, is one of the technologies that is in commercial use. Jennifer Volz, head of global business development at Orbem, said operators are finding that in-ovo sexing improves performance because fewer eggs are wasted on embryos that were never going to contribute to production, setters and hatchers run at higher capacity with female-only eggs, hatch windows are shorter and more uniform, and the bottleneck of manual sexing after hatch is removed. 

According to Volz, the US transition could be quicker than many expect because only 10 to 15 hatcheries would need in-ovo sexing equipment to fully convert the entire US commodity egg market. She described the combination of welfare and operational benefits as one reason adoption is accelerating. The technology also offers potential supply-chain benefits. Male eggs can be removed at or before day 12, freeing up space for female eggs rather than using the same capacity for embryos that will not enter the laying flock. Volz said rejected eggs could become inputs for animal feed, vaccine production or biogas rather than remaining solely a waste stream.

Volz added, “As of June 2026, approximately 40% of the EU's 393 million commercial laying hens had been sexed in-ovo. With more than 200 million eggs scanned across 11 hatcheries in 6 countries, we’re proud to say our Genus Focus played a big role in that achievement.”

PEAK panel member Juliana Machado from Hendrix Genetics stressed, however, that installing equipment is not simply a matter of purchasing a machine. Hatcheries need sufficient space, ventilation, energy supply, trained labour and a workflow that keeps eggs moving through the system. Machado, speaking from a hatchery perspective, said the operational requirements included both infrastructure and skills. Throughput could be sufficient for large hatcheries, but implementation requires layout changes and training.

Developer and user perspective

Vencomatic Group’s involvement in developing the Genus Focus together with Orbem illustrates how equipment companies are approaching the transition. A meeting led to a successful partnership between the companies. Orbem contributed its expertise in MRI and AI, while Vencomatic Group brought decades of experience in egg handling, hatchery logistics and commercial poultry production. That dual role is significant. 

Genus Focus represents a collaboration between a deep-tech company and a poultry equipment company with direct knowledge of hatchery operations. The companies began working together in January 2022, and completed the first installations by the end of that year. Johan Vermeulen, strategic business manager at Vencomatic Group, said the speed of development reflected a start-up-style approach, with rapid testing, prototypes and repeated adjustments. 

For the company, its long experience in egg handling helped the transition. It didn't need to redesign an entire hatchery operation from scratch. translationZh:
关于蛋内性别鉴定的讨论始于蛋品生产中一个令人不安的现实。蛋鸡育种场孵出的雄性雏鸡不产蛋，通常也不适合常规肉鸡生产，因此传统上在孵化后不久即被淘汰。

这项在孵化前识别鸡蛋性别的技术在美国市场仍处于早期阶段，但已不再是假设。特色蛋品生产商开始使用该技术，零售商释放出兴趣信号，行业组织也日益将其视为一个实际问题而非遥远的创新。尚不清楚的是，这项技术能以多快速度从早期采用走向更广泛的行业标准。

相比之下，欧洲在监管和多个市场更强政策压力的推动下走得更远、更快。这种反差正在塑造美国的讨论——美国的采用迄今较少由法律驱动，更多来自零售商预期、生产商战略和消费者反应的混合作用。

**一个福利问题**

在今年早些时候的PEAK 2026小组讨论上，美国防止虐待动物协会（ASPCA）企业政策与动物科学高级总监Nancy Roulston将蛋内性别鉴定称为“终结雄性雏鸡淘汰的解决方案”。她称这是一个罕见的动物福利问题，“完全可预防，且能在短短几年内完全解决”。

原理很直接：在孵化前识别雄性胚胎，并在孵化期更早阶段将其移除。技术挑战在于要可靠、足够快速地确定性别，同时不干扰孵化场运营。这一挑战塑造了市场的发展路径。

美国鸡蛋生产者联合会（United Egg Producers）动物福利副总裁Larry Sadler表示，早期的承诺并不总能转化为商业可行的系统，但该技术现已进步到多家公司可在市场上运营的程度。Innovate Animal Ag项目总监Casey Downey提到3家公司（AAT、Orbem和Seleggt）已推出“在商业上成功且已商业化上市”的系统。另有2家公司加入这3家之列：Omegga和Nectra。

**美国的早期采用**

根据Innovate Animal Ag最新的蛋内性别鉴定市场渗透报告，美国目前有6套商业化蛋内性别鉴定设备在运行，承诺在现有鸡群淘汰后转型的蛋品生产商所代表的蛋鸡存栏占全国蛋鸡存栏的4%以上。

采用蛋内性别鉴定技术孵化出的母鸡所产的鸡蛋，已通过NestFresh的Humanely Hatched标签和Kipster到达美国消费者手中。这些特色蛋品生产商的早期采用帮助该技术进入主流视野，促使大型行业参与者评估其对自己生产方式和品牌定位的潜在影响。截至该报告发布时，包括Sauder's Eggs和Vital Farms在内的其他特色蛋品公司已宣布计划将其鸡群转向蛋内性别鉴定。

早期识别雄性鸡蛋有助于孵化场降低人工成本，并释放宝贵的孵化器和出雏器空间。

NestFresh是最早将蛋内性别鉴定鸡群所产鸡蛋商业化的美国生产商之一。该公司推出了Humanely Hatched品牌，目前正从最初的特色产品线向外扩展。

NestFresh高级副总裁Michael Sencer表示，公司以褐壳蛋为主，这使其天然适合其选择的AAT的Cheggy系统。“Cheggy只适用于褐壳鸡，也是唯一能以更高速度运行以帮助降低成本的产品，”他说。“我们没有因这一工艺而提价。”

他表示，转型需要时间和投资。Sencer补充说，公司计划在2026年底前完成NestFresh及部分特色品牌的蛋内性别鉴定转型，随后再将该方式扩展到自有品牌客户。

**欧洲的进展**

欧洲仍是领先市场。根据市场渗透报告，自2021年以来，全球已有超过2.81亿枚雄性胚胎在孵化前被识别并移除（图1）。在欧盟在产的3.28亿至3.46亿只商业蛋鸡中，有1.25亿至1.42亿只通过蛋内技术进行了性别鉴定，意味着市场渗透率为36.2%至43.3%。这高于2025年4月的34%。这一显著增长恰逢2023年底至2025年中期欧洲蛋内性别鉴定产能的快速扩张。

图1 – 截至2026年6月1日全球蛋内性别鉴定的雄性雏鸡达2.81亿只

蛋内性别鉴定技术在整个欧盟的推广迅速加快，证明其有能力满足一些世界最大产蛋市场的需求。过去4年，使用该技术每年生产的母雏数量以74%的年增长率增长。截至2026年6月的12个月内，蛋内性别鉴定系统生产了9200万只母雏（图2），而装机容量（截至市场渗透报告发布时）超过每年1亿只母雏。

图2 – 欧盟通过蛋内性别鉴定生产的母雏

意大利计划禁止淘汰雄性雏鸡，将成为欧洲蛋内性别鉴定增长的下一个主要驱动力。当该立法于2027年1月生效时，意大利将加入德国和法国的行列，强制要求采用雄性雏鸡淘汰的替代方案，而荷兰则继续其行业主导的转型。这些市场合计占欧盟人口的50.9%。由于新法规仅影响新孵出的雏鸡，转型将随着蛋鸡群在约18个月生产周期内被替换而逐步发生，导致市场渗透率稳步上升而非立即激增。放眼欧洲之外，在2025年启动蛋内性别鉴定技术的瑞士，采用率现已达到该国蛋鸡群的约85%至100%，而挪威已超过50%，并正朝着2027年完全淘汰雄性雏鸡淘汰的方向迈进。

**技术与孵化场效率**

Orbem的AI驱动MRI蛋内性别鉴定系统Genus Focus是已投入商业使用的技术之一。Orbem全球业务发展负责人Jennifer Volz表示，运营者发现蛋内性别鉴定能提升绩效，因为浪费在永远不会参与生产的胚胎上的鸡蛋更少，孵化器和出雏器以全母蛋更高容量运行，孵化窗口更短且更一致，且孵化后人工鉴别的瓶颈被消除。

据Volz称，美国的转型可能比许多人预期的更快，因为只需10至15家孵化场配备蛋内性别鉴定设备，就能完全转化整个美国商品蛋市场。她将福利与运营效益的结合描述为采用加速的原因之一。该技术还带来潜在的供应链效益。雄性鸡蛋可在第12天或之前移除，为雌性鸡蛋腾出空间，而不是将相同容量用于不会进入蛋鸡群的胚胎。Volz表示，被剔除的鸡蛋可作为动物饲料、疫苗生产或沼气的原料，而不再仅仅是废物流。

Volz补充说：“截至2026年6月，欧盟3.93亿只商业蛋鸡中约40%已进行蛋内性别鉴定。在6个国家的11家孵化场扫描超过2亿枚鸡蛋，我们很自豪地说我们的Genus Focus在其中发挥了重要作用。”

另见：随着欧盟采用率达到40%，蛋内性别鉴定势头增强

然而，PEAK小组成员、Hendrix Genetics的Juliana Machado强调，安装设备不仅仅是购买一台机器。孵化场需要足够的空间、通风、能源供应、训练有素的劳动力，以及保持鸡蛋在系统中流动的工作流程。Machado从孵化场角度发言说，运营要求包括基础设施和技能。对于大型孵化场而言吞吐量可能足够，但实施需要布局调整和培训。

**开发者与用户视角**

Vencomatic Group与Orbem共同开发Genus Focus的参与，展示了设备公司如何应对这一转型。一次会议促成了两家公司之间的成功合作。Orbem贡献了其在MRI和AI方面的专业知识，而Vencomatic Group则带来了数十年在鸡蛋处理、孵化场物流和商业家禽生产方面的经验。这种双重角色意义重大。

Genus Focus代表了一家深科技公司与一家直接了解孵化场运营的家禽设备公司之间的合作。两家公司于2022年1月开始合作，并于当年年底完成首批安装。Vencomatic Group战略业务经理Johan Vermeulen表示，开发速度反映了初创企业式的做法，包括快速测试、原型和反复调整。

对该公司而言，其在鸡蛋处理方面的长期经验帮助了转型。它无需从头重新设计整个孵化场运营，而是可以建立在鸡蛋如何从农场交付经过接收、转移、质量控制和孵化等环节的现有知识之上。“管理鸡蛋，尤其是温和对待鸡蛋……”
author: Sunita van Es-Sahota
